motivation: Exploratory isolated-parent results showed that most established offspring were non-adjacent and that almost all non-adjacent first-generation offspring first appeared on recruitment events. Source audit shows recruitment requires local access and, before a daughter exists, social exposure is the only access channel that can be nonlocal. This contract tests that mechanism on untouched synthetic seeds.
social_exposure_definition: Before continuation, for each destination person, compute the share of social-neighbor influence attributable to planted insurgent members, using the same edge influence weight*trust*represented_relationships and planted armed fraction used by the native social-influence process; average by represented destination population.
prediction_protocol: Seed-grouped cross-validation on rooted parent types. Compare intercept, adjacency-only, Euclidean-only, locality-graph, social, geographic-combined, and hybrid logistic models. No destination/origin fixed effects in the primary comparison.

primary_confirmation_gates.social_kernel_direction: At both 90d and 180d, the social model must not have worse log loss than adjacency-only by more than 0.005.
primary_confirmation_gates.social_kernel_material_gain: At at least one of 90d or 180d, social or hybrid must improve on adjacency-only by >=0.01 absolute log loss OR >=0.05 AUC.
primary_confirmation_gates.seed_robustness: At least 6 of 8 seeds must individually have >0.50 non-adjacent fraction among positive rooted-parent offspring when positives exist.

guardrails: No threshold or feature-set changes after fresh-seed outcomes are viewed.
This tests the isolated first-generation reproduction mechanism, not historical transport or a universal spatial law.
A social-kernel result does not imply physical distance is irrelevant; conditional hybrid performance must be reported.
